items.text: Travis Kelce scored his first touchdown of the 2026 NFL season.
items.explanation: The scoring record shows who scored and when.

items.text: The Chiefs' offense was too predictable against the Colts' defense.
items.explanation: “Too predictable” depends on what each viewer expects; no record settles it.

items.text: Kelce's touchdown came in the first quarter.
items.explanation: The play-by-play record shows which quarter each score came in.

items.text: Overtime games are better entertainment than games decided in regulation.
items.explanation: “Better entertainment” is a preference with no single measurable standard.

items.text: Kansas City won 33-30 in overtime.
items.explanation: The final score and overtime result are in the official game record.

items.text: Cameras should cut to Taylor Swift less often during Chiefs games.
items.explanation: “Should” expresses a preference about broadcasts; a record can't settle it.

items.text: A 79-75 record is enough to call this a good season for Cleveland.
items.explanation: “Enough” and “good” depend on what standard a fan uses.

items.text: José Ramírez hit a sixth-inning solo home run to reach 1,000 career RBIs.
items.explanation: The game log records the inning, the play and his career RBI total.

items.text: Ramírez will own every Cleveland batting record before he retires.
items.explanation: “Will” makes a prediction about the future; no present record can settle it.

items.text: Pitching around Ramírez late in the game would have been smarter for the Athletics.
items.explanation: “Smarter” judges a decision that can't be replayed; no record can confirm it.

items.text: A sellout crowd at Progressive Field watched the Guardians rally from a 3-0 deficit.
items.explanation: Attendance and the inning-by-inning score are in the game record.

items.text: Round-number milestones like 1,000 RBIs matter more than single-season totals.
items.explanation: “Matter more” compares two things by a standard that varies from fan to fan.

items.text: The merger of Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery was valued at $110 billion.
items.explanation: The deal's announced value is in the transaction record.

items.text: Paramount would have lost the case if it had gone to trial.
items.explanation: A trial that never happened has no recorded result, so this can only be a judgment.

items.text: A group of 12 state attorneys general sued to block the merger.
items.explanation: The lawsuit filing lists the states that brought it.

items.text: Combining Paramount and Warner Bros. will give viewers more choice.
items.explanation: “Will give more choice” is a prediction about the future that no record can confirm yet.

items.text: The settlement set a $30 million fee for each film Paramount misses in its release target.
items.explanation: The fee is written into the settlement terms.

items.text: Paramount agreed to freeze the merger while the legal challenge was pending.
items.explanation: The freeze agreement is part of the court record.

items.text: A president should be able to decide which outlets send reporters inside the White House.
items.explanation: “Should be able to” is a view about who ought to control access; a record can't settle it.

items.text: Trump's Truth Social post named CNN, MS NOW and Politico.
items.explanation: The post itself is the record of which outlets it named.

items.text: Cutting a news outlet's White House access over its coverage goes too far.
items.explanation: “Too far” depends on where a person draws the line.

items.text: The announcement came on a Friday.
items.explanation: The date of the post and the Oval Office remarks is on the record.

items.text: CNN and Politico will take the dispute to court.
items.explanation: “Will” is a prediction about what happens next; nothing recorded settles it yet.

items.text: CNN said its reporters were still working in the White House on the evening of the announcement.
items.explanation: CNN's statement is on the record, so what it said can be checked.

items.text: The Bills beat the Lions 41-31 on Thursday night.
items.explanation: The final score and date are in the official game record.

items.text: The Lions' defense was unprepared for Buffalo's offense.
items.explanation: “Unprepared” is a judgment; a game record can't settle it.

items.text: Josh Allen opened the scoring with a 1-yard touchdown run.
items.explanation: The scoring summary lists each score in order.

items.text: The Bills will make the playoffs this season.
items.explanation: “Will” is a prediction; the season hasn't finished.

items.text: Buffalo scored on each of its first four drives.
items.explanation: The drive chart records how each possession ended.

items.text: Josh Allen is the most exciting quarterback in the NFL to watch.
items.explanation: “Most exciting” depends on each viewer's taste.

items.text: RemoveMacAI is an open-source command-line tool.
items.explanation: The project's public repository shows its format and source code.

items.text: Apple should let people turn off Apple Intelligence with a single switch.
items.explanation: “Should” expresses a product-design preference.

items.text: In macOS 27, Apple removed the toggle that turned off Apple Intelligence entirely.
items.explanation: The operating system's settings can be checked directly.

items.text: Giving up AI features is a fair trade for 12GB of extra storage.
items.explanation: “Fair trade” depends on how much each person values the features and the space.

items.text: Apple will bring the master toggle back in a later update.
items.explanation: “Will” is a prediction about Apple's future plans.

items.text: Installing a third-party tool like this is riskier than it looks.
items.explanation: “Riskier than it looks” is a judgment about risk with no single measure.
